title: A speech bubble with a real shadow
summary: A ::after tail made from a rotated square, and filter: drop-shadow so one shadow follows the whole shape.
explanation: The tail is a ::after pseudo-element: a small square in the bubble's colour, positioned at the bottom edge and rotated 45 degrees so only a triangle pokes out. No extra markup is needed.

box-shadow is always the shape of the box, so on the first bubble the tail has no shadow and the shadow ends in a straight line under it. filter: drop-shadow() works on the painted pixels instead, so on the second bubble one shadow traces the bubble and the tail together.
drop-shadow takes no spread value and no inset, and it is applied to the bubble including its pseudo-elements. That is why it goes on .bubble, not on ::after.
tryThis: Remove the transform from .bubble::after: the tail becomes a square sticking out.
Move the tail to the left side: set left: -8px, top: 20px and remove bottom.
Give the second bubble a box-shadow as well and compare the two shadows on the tail.

children.text: box-shadow: the tail has no shadow.
drop-shadow: one shadow for the whole shape.
